subject: dental-hygiene
intro: Dental hygiene leads to the preventive side of oral health: the clinicians who clean and assess, the assistants who keep the chair running, the dentists who diagnose, and the educators who carry prevention into the community.

roles.title: Dental Hygienists
roles.what: Administer oral hygiene care to patients: assess oral hygiene problems and needs, maintain health records, advise patients on disease prevention, and provide advanced care such as fluoride treatment or topical anaesthesia.
roles.where: This is the course's core profession — the hygiene process of care unit covers assessment and planning, instrumentation, and evaluation, while periodontology supplies the disease classification you chart daily.

roles.title: Dental Assistants
roles.what: Perform limited clinical duties under a dentist's direction: prepare and sterilise equipment, ready patients for treatment, assist during procedures, and give patients instructions for oral healthcare, often alongside scheduling and records work.
roles.where: The preventive dentistry unit's sealants and fluoride science, the microbiology behind instrument sterilisation, and oral hygiene instruction are precisely the clinical duties assistants carry out.

roles.title: Dentists, General
roles.what: Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases, injuries and malformations of teeth and gums, treat problems of nerve and pulp that affect oral hygiene and tooth retention, fit dental appliances, and provide preventive care.
roles.where: Head and neck anatomy, oral embryology and histology, and the periodontal assessment you learn here are the diagnostic foundation dental school builds on; many hygienists take this route after years in the chair.

roles.title: Community Health Workers
roles.what: Promote health within a community by helping individuals adopt healthy behaviours, advocate for their health needs, and implement programmes that maintain and improve community health, sometimes delivering preventive screenings.
roles.where: The community and professional practice unit — public health dental hygiene, ethics and law, evidence-based practice — is the exact toolkit for taking oral health promotion beyond the clinic.
